LESSON: WRITING 7.3.1 WRITING FOR INFORMATION

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.3: Writing 7.3.1 Writing for information
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 7.3.1 Writing for information, part of Strand 7 in Grade 7 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How do we write a paragraph?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read varied paragraphs related to the theme with peers,

2. work with peers to discuss the parts of a paragraph,

3. prepare sentence strips to form a coherent paragraph,

4. work with peers to reorganise the jumbled-up sentence strips to form a coherent paragraph,

5. use topic sentences to begin paragraphs and complete the story,

6. peer review each other’s topical paragraphs.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read varied paragraphs related to the theme with peers,
2. work with peers to discuss the parts of a paragraph,
3. prepare sentence strips to form a coherent paragraph,
4. work with peers to reorganise the jumbled-up sentence strips to form a coherent paragraph,
5. use topic sentences to begin paragraphs and complete the story,
6. peer review each other’s topical paragraphs.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 7.3.1 Writing for information together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and Imagination: This is developed as the learner explores new ideas when using topic sentences to begin

paragraphs and complete the story.

• Citizenship: This is promoted as the learner shows tolerance and expresses different viewpoints when peer reviewing

each other’s topical paragraphs.

Values:
• Love: This is promoted as the learner selflessly works with peers to reorganise the jumbled-up sentence strips to form

a coherent paragraph.

• Respect: This is cultivated as the learner appreciates diverse opinions when working with peers to discuss the parts of a

paragraph.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Career education is promoted as the learner interacts with texts on the theme of gifts and talents and relates them with

various career opportunities.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can link the concept of paragraph writing to their learning of creative writing in English and Kiswahili.
